newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses close at new peaks on rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses close at new peaks on rate hopes.

text.p: Major European bourses shot to new closing records on Wednesday as investors became convinced that interest rates in the influential U.S. economy would remain on hold.

On foreign exchanges, the dollar set a new four-year high against the yen and probed back above 1.65 marks in Europe as meetings of the Group of Seven industrial nations (G7) and the U.S. Federal Reserve helped underpin the American currency.
In London, stocks finished at a new peak of 4281.5 points after the Bank of England signalled no change in interest rates, beating the previous best set last month.
Few had anticipated a rate hike, but the risk of a surprise kept the market on edge, dealers said.

Traders were still waiting for the outcome of a session of the U.S. central bank's policy-making committee on interest rates. The Federal Open Markets committee makes its announcement at 1915 GMT tonight though no change in monetary policy is expected in the U.S. either.

Recent economic statistics in the U.S. continue to show non-inflationary growth whilst in Britain economists expect finance minister Kenneth Clarke to continue to resist rate rises at such a politically-sensitive time. The British government has to call a general election by late May.
But meanwhile, Wall Street made a good start on Wednesday, climbing 0.25 percent, further cheering European bourses.
Yet some investors remained on edge ahead of London's reporting season as some companies have been hit by the appreciation in sterling on the foreign exchange markets.
"The (price/earnings) ratings in this market are very demanding and we really do need to see the proof that the market's optimism is merited by the results," said a trader.
In Frankfurt, floor trading closed at a new peak of 3098.0 on the DAX index boosted by the strength of the dollar trading above 1.64 marks, which was soon as boosted export prospects.

"There is strong support there from the dollar and the focus is very much on individual stocks, although the chemical sector is strong because of the dollar. The specific interest this morning is on Lufthansa ," said one trader.
In Paris, French stocks rallied to a record close on the dollar's strength and expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will not raise U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 38.18 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,541.25, surpassing the previous closing record set last Friday of 2,516.56 points.
"There's a feeling that the Fed will hold still for the time being," a trader said.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened on growing optimism about interest rates and the G7 finance ministers meeting on Saturday in Berlin.
Official comments ahead of the meeting suggest they will broadly endorse the recent rise of the dollar while shunning excess volatility.

The Federal Open Market Committee met for the second day today, meantime. While no change in interest rates is expected, the outside chance of a rate rise has kept traders from pushing the dollar two far from recent ranges.

"The dollar is basically just idling around the place, with a degree of nervousness about the Fed, G7 and the January (U.S.) payrolls keeping it buoyed up," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
Ferridge said surprisingly weak German industrial orders data on Wednesday and expectations of a weak January German unemployment report early tomorrow kept a lid on the mark.

The dollar was at 123.50 yen in late afternoon trade, a fresh four-year high and well above its late Tuesday European level of 122.30. Against the mark, it was at 1.6473 compared with 1.6424 on Tuesday.

The mark got a boost earlier from a Financial Times report that Italy would be offered a compromise deal to delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001. An EU official said such a plan was being considered "in some quarters".
"Initially, dollar/mark was depressed today because there was a lot of mark buying against the lira on the news about EMU," the bank trader said.

"It's the contrast between very strong growth in the U.S. and weak growth in Japan and Europe that is driving the dollar higher, and there's nothing on the horizon that's going to change that," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.6473 marks and 123.50 yen in late European trade after closing in Europe at 1.6424 marks and 122.30 yen on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 20.6 points higher at 4,281.5
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index finished up 30.94 points higher at 3,098.00.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended up 38.18 at 2,541.25.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $342.95 an ounce after ending in Europe on Tuesday at $346.30.
